summary: Created opsbot on both nodes and configured node1→node2 SSH access using an ED25519 key generated on node1. Both systems enforce public-key-only authentication for opsbot. The configuration and access survived sequential reboots of both nodes. CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created locked-password opsbot accounts on node1 and node2.
Generated opsbot's SSH keypair on node1 and installed its public key on node2.
Configured and validated per-user public-key-only sshd policy on both nodes.
Verified node1 executes commands on node2 as opsbot and that no-key authentication is rejected by both systems.
Restarted node1 and node2 one at a time, confirmed changed boot identities, and verified service, policy, key data, and end-to-end access recovery.

evidence.requirement: Create opsbot accounts and provision node1's key access to node2
evidence.summary: Shows account creation, node1 key generation, node2 authorized-key installation, and restrictive ownership and permissions.

evidence.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems
evidence.summary: Effective sshd policy requires publickey and disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication; no-key attempts are rejected with Permission denied (publickey).

evidence.requirement: Run commands as opsbot from node1 on node2
evidence.summary: Before and after both reboots, node1 authenticated without password fallback, ran as opsbot uid 1000 on node2, and created opsbot-owned files.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64; no software installation or OS/kernel replacement occurred.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 34e2e001-9535-48ee-9a4c-84e6593cca9c, recovered sshd/policy/key data, and restored node1→node2 access.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID 5e93a57c-0d8d-454e-8fb1-617b2a46810c, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 2c6e198a-9bab-485d-910a-df874b3c238e, recovered sshd/policy/authorized-key data, and successful end-to-end key access after both restarts.
